description.value: The study investigated how schizophrenia and chronic cannabis use affect behavioral and neural sensitivity to reward anticipation during a two-choice reaction-time task performed during fMRI.

design.value: A 2 × 2 group design compared cannabis use and schizophrenia status, with reward condition as a within-subject factor; age and years of education were continuous covariates. Behavioral analyses included 83 participants and imaging analyses included 73 participants.

description.value: Pattern of cannabis use was gathered via self-report measures.

task_description.value: A two-choice RT task was used with elements of the MID and Eriksen flanker tasks. Participants responded to the pointing direction of the central arrowhead after valence and magnitude cues while being scanned using functional magnetic resonance imaging.

instructions.value: The participant was informed that the aim of the task was to gain a maximal amount of points and in order for them to win (+) or avoid losing (–), they must respond both accurately and quickly.

stimuli.value: Five arrow heads appearing for a fixed period; only the incongruent configuration was used.

instrument.value: Philips Achieva 3.0 Tesla TX MRI scanner

description.value: Functional MR images were acquired using echo-planar imaging with 36 slices and 3 × 3 × 3 mm voxel size. A high-resolution T1 anatomical image with 1 × 1 × 1 mm voxel size was also acquired for each participant.

instrument.value: Philips Achieva 3.0 Tesla TX MRI scanner

description.value: A high-resolution T1 anatomical image with 1 × 1 × 1 mm voxel size was acquired for each participant.

Pre-processing was first performed by spatially realigning the raw images and temporal interpolation was completed to correct for delay in slice acquisition. The T1 image was next used to segment the images into grey and white matter and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Images were normalized to standard Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space and smoothed with an 8 mm full width at half maximum (FWHM) Gaussian kernel. A high-pass filter of 128 s cut off was applied.

model_settings.value: Three regressors, reward (+), punishment (−) and neutral (*) were included for the valence model. Five regressors (−20, −5, 0, +5, +20) were included for the magnitude model. Additional regressors included motion correction parameters estimated from the realignment step. T-contrasts were calculated.

The main analysis was a 2 × 2 ANCOVA to assess the modulation of each contrast with cannabis use, schizophrenia status and their interaction, with years of education and age as covariates. ROI analyses used family-wise error correction adjusted for small volume at p < 0.05 and a minimum cluster size of three contiguous voxels.

A 2 × 2 × 5 analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) design was used, with reward condition as the within-subject repeated measures factor, cannabis use and schizophrenia as between-group fixed factors, and education level and age as continuous covariates.

interpretations.value: Extraction of beta values showed an increased activation in the right putamen, ventral anterior insula and dorsal anterior insula for reward versus punishment for cannabis users (HC + C and SZ + C) compared to non-users (HC−C and SZ−C).

footer.value: Duration, frequency and age of first use for HC−C and SZ−C were not reported since most of them did not use cannabis. Lifetime use is an estimation based on duration and frequency of use. All measures apart from sex are equivalent to the mean of the respective group. Parentheses indicate standard deviation. Bold typeface = p < 0.05. p values for all cannabis use variables indicate significance for testing differences between HC + C and SZ + C. HC−C non-cannabis user healthy controls, HC + C cannabis-user healthy controls, SZ−C non-cannabis user schizophrenia patients, SZ + C cannabis-user schizophrenia patients. a Analysis of variance (ANOVA) was used. b Chi-square test was used. c Independent samples t-test was used.
